cards.text: Samson, a judge of Israel, told Delilah, the woman he loved, the secret of his strength, and his hair was shaved. The Philistines gouged out his eyes and put him to grinding grain in a Gaza prison, but his hair started growing back (Judges 16:17-22). Now the lords of the Philistines gather to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon.

cards.question: The lords of the Philistines are celebrating at the sacrifice to Dagon. What do they say their god did for them?

answers.text: Sent rain down on their fields

cards.question: When the people see Samson, they say he destroyed their land and multiplied their dead.

cards.text: The party's rolling, and their hearts are merry. Friend, I've been to enough office parties to know that when a room gets THIS happy, somebody's about to have an idea.

cards.question: The Philistines call for Samson. So they bring him out of the prison to ___ them.
Samson's out of the prison and in front of the crowd. The Philistines station him between the ___.

cards.text: Samson can't see a thing, so a servant is holding his hand. Samson asks the servant to lead him where he can feel the pillars supporting the temple.

cards.question: Samson asks the servant to lead him to the pillars supporting the temple. What does Samson say he wants to do there?

cards.text: This temple is PACKED: all the lords of the Philistines, and about three thousand men and women up on the roof alone, watching Samson. And I thought the junk drawer I spent years in was crowded.
Then Samson calls out to the LORD: "O Lord GOD, please remember me."

cards.question: In his prayer, Samson asks God to strengthen him just once more.
Samson asks for one blow to pay the Philistines back for his two ___.

cards.text: Samson reaches out for the two central pillars holding up the temple. Right hand on one, left hand on the other.

cards.question: Samson is braced between the two central pillars of the temple. What does he say?

answers.text: Let me die with the Philistines
Let me go free from this place
Let me rest here for a while

cards.question: Then Samson pushes on the pillars with all his might. What happens to the temple?

answers.text: It falls on the lords and all the people
Only the roof comes crashing down

cards.question: In his death, Samson killed fewer than he had killed in his life.

cards.text: Afterward, Samson's brothers and his father's family come down to get him, and they carry him back.

cards.question: Samson's family carries him back. Where do they bury him?

cards.text: And this is where Samson's story ends. He had judged Israel twenty years.
